_comment: Sound cue catalogue (9 Nov 2026), read by scripts/core/sound.gd. cues: id -> file, bus (default_bus_layout.tres), volume_db, loop (the file's .import loop_mode must match), distance (unit_size / max_distance in metres), source, licence. restart (optional): a new play stops the same cue still sounding at that node. A cue with no distance is flat (sound.gd play_ui). bindings: scripts whose signals (no arguments) play cues; objects stay silent themselves. Doors are not bound: door_animator.gd plays door.<kind>.open / .close (25 Nov 2026). Record: docs/guides/TOWN_DESIGN_BRIEF.md 'Bathroom fixtures'.

buttons._comment: Button sounds (25 Nov 2026, user: a sound for confirm and decline, then every kind of button; each picked by ear). BonStyle tags each button it styles with meta bon_kind; sound.gd plays this map's cue for that kind when the button is pressed (flat, play_ui). A button's meta 'sound' overrides it (a cue id, or 'none' for silence; the dialogue's 'no' choice uses ui.decline). Buttons BonStyle never styled (touch controls, game pieces) stay silent.

music._comment: Background music (25 Nov 2026, user: a lofi BGM for the demo, and a different soundtrack for the loading screen). tracks: name -> cue; sound.gd play_music(name) fades the playing track out over 'fade_out' s and the new one in over 'fade_in' s, on its cue's bus, not positional. App plays 'loading' with the loading screen and 'town' when it lifts. A minigame plays its activities.json 'music' track while it runs and the town track after (25 Nov 2026, user: different songs for different activities). Each cue's volume_db evens out the tracks' loudness (about -26.5 dB average with the cue's volume). 'enabled' false silences all music. Placeholders until licensed or commissioned music. Checks (a SceneTree script) never play it.

voice._comment: Spoken words (24 Nov 2026): one clip per word and language at <folder>/<lang>/<file>.ogg, where <file> is sound.gd voice_file(key). 'enabled' is the master switch: while false, sound.gd say_word() plays nothing. Switched on 24 Nov 2026 (user). tools/voice_manifest.gd lists what to say; tools/voice_generate.py makes the clips with Amazon Polly. 'languages' gives each language's Polly voice. Guide: docs/guides/VOICE.md.
